newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HKTel fights for speedy OK on tariff cuts.
newsitem.headline: HKTel fights for speedy OK on tariff cuts.

text.p: Hongkong Telecom (HKT) on Wednesday criticised the telecommunications authority for acting too slowly to approve tariff cuts.
The Office of the Telecommunications Authority (OFTA) is now mulling a list of HKT proposals to cut tariffs, including a plan to give discounts on some international routes in December.

"It is disappointing that in spite of HKT's cooperation in putting Hong Kong in the forefront of international liberalisation that the tariff approval processes proposed by OFTA are themselves not fully in line with international regulatory practise even in countries which are much less liberal than Hong Kong," HKT said in a statement.
"The 'slow track' approach on volume discounts, product packaging and price reductions is unwarranted given the state of competition," it said.

HKT is up against stiff competition from companies like New T&T, the telecommunications arm of Wharf (Holdings) Ltd, New World Telephone, owned by New World Development Ltd and Hutchison Telephone, a unit of Hutchison Whampoa Ltd.
HKT also urged that "a less timid approach is required to quickly bring the full benefits of competition to the public".
